title: SPPD - Local police data sharing with other agencies

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: SPPD - Local police data sharing with other agencies
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting records showing which outside systems receive Saint Paul Police Department records, and which outside agencies or companies can search them:

1. Any contract, agreement, addendum, order form or invoice between the City of Saint Paul or the Police Department and LexisNexis Risk Solutions, including Accurint for Law Enforcement, the Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), Community Crime Map, LexisNexis Coplogic, and any "Schedule A" or "AVCC XML Addendum" covering the sending of incident data to LexisNexis.

2. Any agreement, memorandum of understanding or user agreement for CrimeTracer (Forensic Logic, now SoundThinking), the FBI's National Data Exchange (N-DEx), LInX, COPLINK, or any similar multi-agency system that receives or searches the Department's incident, arrest, field contact or case records.

3. Any memorandum of understanding, joint powers agreement or data-sharing agreement under which Department records are sent to another agency's system, including Ramsey County (a shared records management or dispatch system, or the Ramsey County Sheriff's Office), the Minnesota BCA (including CIBRS), and the Minnesota Fusion Center.

4. For each system covered by items 1 to 3, the most recent participant list, member agency list or access roster showing which agencies or organizations can access Department data. Agency names are enough; I do not need individual user names.

For context: the Ramsey County Sheriff's Office and several neighboring departments send incident records to LexisNexis, and the Department's policy manual (sections 238.00 and 239.00) describes access to BCA systems including CIBRS. I am trying to understand where St. Paul PD's records go and who can search them. Signed agreements, schedules, invoices and participant lists will answer this; I am not asking for emails or PII. 

Time range: January 1, 2018 through the date of fulfillment. Please send electronic copies by email or download link.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal
